correctionsTheBuildForced: P-330's first test run failed for a reason that was a REAL defect, not a test artifact: the runner assigned its `lastExecution`/`lastJob` bookkeeping even when a child had failed, so a stopped step's record was priced and written as `succeeded`/`refused` instead of `failed`. The tests caught it; the fix moved the assignment inside the success branch. Stated because 'the test was wrong' and 'the code was wrong' are different diagnoses and this was the second.

P-330's fake Cloud Run had to key its executions map by the SHORT execution name (the last path segment), because that is the name the runner waits on -- the first version keyed the full resource name and every fail case looked like a pass. This is a fact about the runner's interface that a reader of the test file now inherits.

P-330's case-4 test (declared code from a DIFFERENT job) was originally pointed at factory-dollar-fields-patch, which declares nothing at all -- so 'not declared for this job' was being measured against a job with no declarations, a weaker fact than intended. It was re-pointed at factory-parcel-max-impervious-cover, which declares COUNTY_NOT_IN_SCOPE: the code under test is now declared FOR ANOTHER JOB and is still refused. The direct declaredScopeRefusalFor assertion below it was re-pointed with it.

P-330's step-6 test had to pass --clear-ruling-stop: stage 6 carries the `ruling` stop point, so a walk started at stage 6 stops at it before the rail-fill step runs (the ruling stop is not a refusal and not this row's subject).

P-329: the new fixture tests were ADDED TO the ldt-sha-comment-presence CI job, not only to `npm test`. Both run them (package.json's test glob covers test/*.test.mjs), but the job wired to the check is where a future reader looks for what pins the check down.

secretListAuditResultForP334: Exactly ONE other job in cloudbuild.publish.yaml has the mirrored shape, and it is one step worse: `factory-verify-walk` mounts SECRETS=FACTORY_DATABASE_URL only and sets STAGING_SITE_URL, while src/jobs/verify-walk.mjs's loadCountyJurisdictions resolves the target PAIR (`resolveTargetStores(env, "staging")`, destructuring DATABASE_URL) -- so on the deployed job neither STAGING_NEONDB_URL nor STAGING_HAUSKA_MCP_URL exists and the walk's own resolver refuses. The remaining five deploy cases were read against their jobs' resolvers and are consistent: factory-publish-migrate (migrate: factory store only), factory-staging-reset (factory + NEON_API_KEY, no target resolver), factory-bastrop-publish and factory-dollar-fields-patch (both mount BOTH targets' pairs, which is what resolveTargetStores demands), factory-republish-on-change (mounts the two mcp urls it reads and no database url -- it never calls a target-store resolver). The mismatch is asserted as a fact about today's template in test/p334-watch-secret-mount.test.mjs and NOT fixed here: whether factory-verify-walk should narrow its resolver (it reads only DATABASE_URL from that call) or widen its mount is a decision about a different job's contract.
adjacencyDefinitionForP329: PIN_COMMENT_ADJACENCY_LINES = 3, declared once in scripts/check-ldt-sha-comment-presence.mjs. An added comment line counts only if its line number in the NEW file (the file a reader opens, taken from the hunk header -- not arithmetic on diff offsets) is within 3 lines of the added `_LDT_SHA:` line, either side. A real comment is `^\s*#.*\S`: a bare `#` spacer is not a provenance note. WHY 3, with its basis: the CTX-PIN convention this checks places a provenance comment immediately above the substitution it describes (see the CTX-PIN2/CTX-PIN4 blocks in cloudbuild.publish.yaml itself), sometimes two lines of it, sometimes with a blank line between; 3 admits the comment, its continuation line and one blank or `substitutions:`-level neighbour, and excludes a comment block describing another substitution -- which is the failure this closes. It is a constant, not a flag: a wider window re-opens the hole, a narrower one (0 or 1) refuses the real CTX-PIN shape, which would get the guard turned off. The boundary is measured at 3 (PASS) and 4 (FAIL) in the test file.
